text:
Abstract
We queried NCBI GEO for Series accession GSE309890 to determine the study’s topic and the downloadable processed data files. Using the GEO Series retrieval tool with accession=GSE309890 and list_files=true, we obtained curated metadata: the title, summary, organism, experiment type, platform, sample count, per-sample GSM identifiers, BioProject, GEO page URL, and FTP directories. We also enumerated supplementary files from the GEO FTP “suppl” directory. The study focuses on Escherichia coli K-12 MG1655 under selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) exposure (sertraline) and reports that sertraline biases antibiotic resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway, with transketolase A (tktA) implicated. The experiment type is expression profiling by high-throughput sequencing (RNA-seq), with 6 samples and platform GPL24659. One downloadable processed file is listed: GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz (510K; last modified 2025-11-14). No PubMed record is linked to the Series at the time of retrieval. These results identify the study’s scope and provide exact URLs to download processed expression values, enabling immediate use in downstream analyses.

I. Introduction
Background. GSE309890 is a GEO Series reporting RNA-seq expression profiling in Escherichia coli K-12 MG1655 under sertraline exposure. The summary describes sertraline-induced bias in antibiotic resistance emergence through redox stress and pentose phosphate pathway rewiring, with transketolase A (tktA) modulating susceptibility.
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.
Knowledge Gap. Before the query, the specific focus of GSE309890 and the availability/location of downloadable processed files were not enumerated.
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: retrieve the curated description of GSE309890 and list the downloadable processed data files. Hypothesis: GEO metadata will provide the study’s summary and FTP-based links to supplementary processed expression files.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. We targeted NCBI GEO because Series records centralize study metadata and processed expression files. The GEO Series tool returns both the curated Series record and its FTP “suppl” directory listing.
Materials.
- NCBI GEO (functions.geo_series).
Procedures.
- functions.geo_series(accession="GSE309890", list_files=true).
  - Returned: record metadata (accession, title, summary, taxon, experiment_type, date_public, platform, sample_count, samples, BioProject), GEO page URL, FTP directory URL, supplementary directory URL, and enumerated supplementary files.
- Provenance (as returned): esummary.fcgi URL with params db=gds, id=200309890, version=2.0; GEO page; FTP Series directory; FTP suppl directory; individual file URL.
Statistical Analysis.
- Sample count (n=6) taken directly from record.sample_count.
- Supplementary file count (n=1) computed as the length of supplementary_files list.
- File size and timestamp taken from supplementary_files.size and supplementary_files.last_modified, respectively.
- No deduplication was required; lists were reported as returned.

III. Results
Data Presentation.
Table 1. Study metadata and links
| Field                     | Value                                                                 |
|--------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Accession                | GSE309890                                                              |
| Entry type               | Series (GSE)                                                           |
| Title                    | Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway: tktA enables metabolic rollback |
| Summary                  | Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) may accelerate antibiotic resistance… (full text in record) |
| Organism                 | Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655                              |
| Experiment type          | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing                     |
| Date public              | 2026/02/01                                                             |
| Platform                 | GPL24659                                                               |
| Sample count             | 6                                                                      |
| Samples (GSM)            | GSM9284462; GSM9284459; GSM9284457; GSM9284460; GSM9284461; GSM9284458 |
| BioProject               | PRJNA1363958                                                           |
| PubMed link              | None linked                                                            |
| GEO page URL             | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890          |
| FTP directory            | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/           |
| Supplementary directory  | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/     |
| Supplementary types      | CSV                                                                    |

Table 2. Downloadable supplementary files
| File name                          | Size  | Last modified         | URL                                                                                                                   |
|------------------------------------|-------|------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz  | 510K  | 2025-11-14 11:10       | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz                  |

Findings.
- The Series describes RNA-seq expression profiling in E. coli K-12 MG1655 with sertraline-induced resistance bias.
- Six samples are listed.
- One processed supplementary file is available (FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz, 510K).
- No PubMed link is registered.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. GSE309890 is an RNA-seq study of sertraline’s impact on antibiotic resistance emergence in E. coli via redox/PPP rewiring. The available processed data is a single FPKM matrix file aggregating all samples, downloadable from GEO’s FTP supplementary directory.
Context. The summary reports Complex I-dependent respiratory compensation, oxidative stress, PPP flux, and tktA modulation as central findings. The processed expression file supports quantitative analysis of these pathways across the six samples.
Limitations. GEO’s API provides metadata only; processed matrices exist solely in supplementary files. At retrieval, only one file is listed. No PubMed record is linked in GEO, which does not imply absence of a manuscript but limits citation context here. The Series-level metadata does not enumerate raw sequencing runs.
Conclusion & Future Directions. GSE309890 centers on sertraline-induced metabolic rewiring and antibiotic resistance bias in E. coli. The primary reusable artifact is an all-sample FPKM matrix downloadable from the GEO FTP. Next queries worth running include: retrieving raw sequencing runs via SRA/ENA using the BioProject PRJNA1363958, and checking for additional per-sample files or metadata updates over time. A reusable TSV of the supplementary-file inventory can be generated on request.

References
[1] NCBI GEO Series page: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890
[2] NCBI GEO FTP directory (Series): https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/
[3] NCBI GEO FTP supplementary directory: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/
[4] Supplementary file (FPKMs): https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz
[5] NCBI E-utilities esummary (provenance): https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi

Acknowledgments
We acknowledge NCBI GEO and NCBI E-utilities for the curated Series metadata and FTP file listings.
